_about: Parameters for the Multi-Vital Correlation Engine (T11). Each rule cross-checks two vitals. 'inconsistent' means the pair cannot both be true of a real patient (sensor fault or tampering suspected); 'concerning' means each value may be acceptable on its own but the combination is clinically worrying. Set 'verified' to true once the parameter has been checked against its source.

R-CORR-HR-PULSE.description: ECG-derived heart rate and oximeter pulse rate measure the same heartbeat and should agree.
R-CORR-HR-PULSE.source: Engineering choice, to be justified: largest disagreement tolerated between two sensors measuring the same beat.

R-CORR-SPO2-HR.description: Severe hypoxaemia normally provokes a compensatory tachycardia, so a very low SpO2 alongside a normal heart rate suggests a displaced or faulty oximeter probe (scenario S6).
R-CORR-SPO2-HR.source: To find: physiological reference for compensatory tachycardia in acute hypoxaemia.

R-CORR-SHOCK-INDEX.description: Shock index = heart rate / systolic blood pressure. A value at or above the limit suggests haemodynamic compromise even when HR and BP are individually acceptable.
R-CORR-SHOCK-INDEX.source: Allgower M, Burri C. 'Schockindex'. Dtsch Med Wochenschr. 1967;92(43):1947-1950.

R-CORR-BP-ORDER.description: Diastolic pressure is by definition lower than systolic pressure in the same measurement.
R-CORR-BP-ORDER.source: Definition of systolic and diastolic blood pressure.
